claim: TT policy: uint16 obs -> 4 hex digits/feature -> one core [r,16,r] per digit -> 8 action logits. Impls: numpy gather, numpy digit-bucket, numba prange(3 thr), torch CPU(3 thr), torch GPU end-to-end (H2D obs + D2H int32 actions) and GPU resident. Predict: at batch=1 CPU (numba) beats GPU e2e by >=10x (kernel launch ~3/core); GPU e2e overtakes best CPU at B~1k for r=16,d=16; crossover moves DOWN as r grows (r=64: B<=128) and UP as r shrinks (r=4: >=16k or never to 262k). Oracle: all impls == float64 reference logits (tol 1e-3 rel) and identical argmax off near-ties; positive control = analytically built additive TT; cheat controls = skip-half-cores impl must FAIL oracle, unsynchronised GPU timer must be FLAGGED by wall-clock cross-check.

controls.cheat: skip-half-cores impl invalid in 42/42 cells with >=64 samples compared (59/60 overall; the miss is B=1, one sample); unsynced GPU timer claimed up to 43x resident but wall-clock-with-sync accounting (used for every crossover) gave it <=1.23x at B>=16k; per-call timer flag caught 11/14 false claims (DEFECT, disclosed)
controls.contention: 13 cells host_cpu>60% during lane B burst; d64 r4 and r64 blocks rerun clean and replaced
controls.positive: additive TT with integer logits bit-exact on all 8 honest backends at d16 and d64; 478/478 honest timed cells valid against float64 per-sample oracle

engineering.timing: wall clock with device sync; 3 CPU threads; RTX 5060 Ti; A=8 actions

science.finding: GPU advantage for gather+bmm TT contraction is 1.2-2.9x and memory-bound past B=16k; the representation, not the device, sets the ceiling
science.instrument_defect: per-call timer flag caught 11/14 false no-sync speed claims; not re-tuned post hoc

claim: Plastic TT (online ALS, surprise grow+flush, TT-rounding under memory charge lam=1e-4, rmax 12), d=4 digits, 8 regimes x 120 steps x 512 samples, noise 0.1. Predict: (1) REAL world (exact rank r* cycling 1,4,2,8): steady max rank within +-1 of r* in >=90% of regime cells; spearman(oracle, steady rank) >=0.9 every seed; switch response >=0.9; <=2 false surprises/run. (2) SOFT world (decaying spectra, oracle = charge-rounded true function): order tracks (rho>=0.8) but level sits BELOW oracle: within+-1 in <=50% of cells (data-limited, not charge-limited). (3) plastic uses <=50% of fixed8 params at steady excess MSE <= fixed8+0.01; fixed2 excess MSE >=5x plastic. (4) NULL (all rank 4, fake labels): steady rank spread <=1 every seed. (5) LEAK probe (flag shifted half a period, deterministic replay): leak_flag LEAK 9/9, honest CLEAN + deterministic all; tracking score alone does NOT separate leak (|rho diff| <=0.1 in real). Status: PASS iff (1),(4),(5) hold; KILL if (1) fails.

controls.cheat: leak_flag brain (flushes+grows on regime-flag change, acting only after targets are seen) flagged LEAK by the flag-shift invariance probe 9/9 (3 seeds x real/soft/null); its tracking score was indistinguishable from the honest brain (rho gap <=0.006), so the probe, not the score, caught it. Probe is one-sided: invariance proves the brain ignores this channel only
controls.null: all-rank-4 world with fake labels: steady rank spread 0.0 in 3/3 seeds
controls.positive: honest brains CLEAN and deterministic on replay 18/18; fixed2 under-capacity excess MSE 0.39-0.42 (instrument sees capacity)

science.construct_limit: REAL world targets are exactly low-rank, so rank recovery there is close to guaranteed by TT-rounding; SOFT world is the non-trivial test and only its ORDER prediction held
science.finding: rank tracks regime complexity and reacts to every switch, but the memory charge buys ~3x fewer params at ~10x the steady excess error of a fixed rank-8 brain, and in non-low-rank worlds the learned rank sits below the charge-optimal rank (data-limited)
